Opt-in Enscribe markup in data-table cells (#21)

A parsed prose column

Data-format tables hold data, so cells are literal by default. A parse-columns attribute opts a single prose column into Enscribe inline markup while the data columns stay literal. Long form is used (the cell content carries >, which would end pipe content early). The notes column links, emphasises, cross-refs the figure below, and cites — all parsed; sample and value stay literal.

Table 1. Results — only the notes column parses.
sample value notes
A 3.14 see the docs at the site
B 2.72 compare with figure 1 and (Smith, 2020)
C 1.41 uses inline code and inline math x2

Parsing every cell

With +parse-text, every cell parses — the all-cells opt-in.

Table 2. Every cell parsed.
label detail
emphasised label a link to the site

Explicit opt-out

-parse-text keeps a table literal even if a document-wide default turned parsing on. Here it is literal (no global default set), demonstrating the attribute is accepted and leaves cells untouched.

Table 3. Explicitly literal.
token note
x this *stays* literal and <a https://example.org | this> is not a link
